Poster and Research by Maytal Amona

Investigating the Effects of Circadian Strategies on Sleep Quality and Recovery in Traveling Athletes

Subjective survey-based research on how circadian strategies influence sleep quality and jet lag recovery in athletes who travel.

Tap the poster to zoom

Abstract

Despite increasing recognition of the importance of sleep in athletic performance, effective strategies to prevent circadian misalignment remain unclear, as circadian strategies influence sleep, jet lag recovery, and performance in frequently traveling athletes. Furthermore, it is unknown if athletes who use circadian strategies experience better outcomes compared to those who do not. Athletes invest many hours of training to reach peak performance; however, traveling across time zones impairs their performance because of jet lag. Thus making sleep and recovery vital to athletes.

To address this issue, I designed a survey to examine how different factors affect sleep and jet lag in traveling athletes. Athletes nationwide were asked to complete the survey to acquire a wide range of responses. The diverse responses from the survey will help make the results more reliable and relevant, reflecting a broader range of athletic backgrounds.

The study found that jet lag is a common issue among athletes, with typical symptoms like trouble falling asleep, daytime fatigue, and waking up too early. These results suggest that traveling across time zones makes it more challenging for athletes to maintain a healthy sleep-wake cycle, which can negatively impact their recovery and athletic performance. Moreover, the effectiveness of circadian strategies for improving athletic performance and sleep varied among participants, signifying that circadian strategies may depend on personal factors, like consistency or their chronotype. Future research can focus on creating an accessible platform to guide athletes on using circadian strategies by providing practical, individualized recommendations. This would improve sleep quality and allow them to perform at their fullest potential.
